absent: Layout and locking of live resource tree, crash image descriptor, boot parameter block and firmware entry structures beyond fields referenced in these fragments.
Implementation of resource walking, memmap callbacks, range exclusion, entry insertion, header preparation and kexec buffer allocation.
Exact trigger encoding values and firmware binding for IOAPIC and processor nodes, plus SMP and NUMA registration contracts.
Concurrency rules for exception stack tables, device tree globals, e820 tables and oops state beyond the die lock variables shown.
Error handling and fallback sources for flattened tree verification and platform bus probing when nodes are missing.
Physical memory layout guarantees for low reservation, crash regions and mailbox placement.

findings.text: Crash memmap builder populates boot parameters from live resource walks and crash reservations, filtering tiny fragments and reporting allocation or exclusion failures.
Crash segment loader prepares program headers, registers them as a kexec buffer with required alignment, records addresses and sizes, and enlarges reservation for hotplug when configured.
Hotplug support query returns affirmative for file based images, otherwise reflects whether caller flags request core header exclusion for updates.
Core header size helper derives reservation from base descriptors plus processor and memory range allowances scaled by program header extent.
Hotplug event handler rebuilds core headers after topology change, validates fit in reserved space, maps destination, invalidates global image during cached copy, then restores and releases scratch.
Old memory reader for legacy paging validates the supplied frame, maps it locally, copies the requested slice into the callers iterator, then unmaps and returns transferred length.
Long mode old memory readers share a common worker that selects encrypted or cached mapping per request, copies the slice, unmaps, with thin wrappers for plain and encrypted paths.
Core header reader adapts a flat buffer into an iterator and delegates to the old memory service, propagating guest memory encryption state.
Boot data hook records the address of firmware setup payload derived from supplied base, backed by early data globals for tree pointer, command line and IOAPIC flag.
Host bridge lookup scans firmware PCI nodes for a bus range whose minimum matches the queried bus number, returning the node or null when absent.
Device tree PCI interrupt setup installs platform hooks; enable skips devices without a pin, otherwise maps firmware interrupt and assigns it, while disable is a no op.

Early tree configuration temporarily maps and verifies the flattened blob, expands mapping when total size exceeds initial window, unflattens a copy, releases mapping, and selects tree based SMP parsing when firmware tables are disabled.

Double fault entry captures faulting address, restores normal task state, marks interrupt tracking off, synthesizes a register frame from task fields, invokes the high level fault handler, then terminates because return is impossible.
Fatal trap reporter opens an oops region, emits a header, invokes an address sanity hook when an address is present, runs body logic to decide signal suppression, then closes the region.
Memory map queries test whether an interval is covered by firmware or current tables and report covering entry type, with an error when coverage is incomplete.
Firmware table importer adds each supplied range to the current map, signals fallback when empty, and aborts remaining entries on address wrap.

Change tracking record pairs a pointer to the original map entry with a boundary address; helpers include a doubled pointer array for sorting, an overlap list and a staging area sized from the maximum entry count.
Exception stack page descriptor holds offset and size plus type tag; a cache aligned table indexed by frame number covers dedicated stacks for fault and trap classes.
IOAPIC trigger descriptor records output kind plus level and polarity flags; a small static table enumerates falling edge, high level, low level and rising edge combinations.
Device tree IRQ domain operations reuse common free and activation helpers while providing a custom allocator that translates firmware cells through the trigger table.
Three parallel map instances represent the active view, the kexec view and the firmware view, each with a global pointer initialized to dedicated early storage.

Memmap construction reserves a few spare slots for header growth and splits, walks low memory and firmware table areas with distinct types, adds low crash reservation, excludes the main crash region keeping only page sized pieces, appends contiguous memory ranges, then frees scratch.

Hotplug reservation accounts for base descriptors plus processor count and optionally range count; processor only changes are skipped when headers already describe all possible processors or when file mode or prior update makes refresh redundant.

Zero length copies succeed without mapping; legacy paging rejects frames whose round trip through page table helpers mismatches; long mode fails cleanly when mapping is unavailable and honors encrypted versus cached selection.

Per processor firmware nodes contribute hardware identifiers with invalid firmware identifiers and NUMA affinity, skipping entries lacking identifiers; local APIC address defaults then honors firmware override, force enables when feature missing else registers, marks SMP config found and derives compatibility mode from a property.

Timer address is adopted when its node exists; wake mailbox requires exact alignment and exact size else ignored and disables processor offlining before firmware handoff, with a configuration fallback that reports unsupported; each IOAPIC node is registered with a fresh identifier and dynamic domain, setting a global flag when any succeed, with an empty fallback when disabled.

Coverage test scans the active table, ignores mismatched types and disjoint entries, advances the uncovered start past each covering prefix, and succeeds when start reaches the end; change point ordering sorts by address with region ends after starts at equal addresses.
Fatal path serialization uses an arch spin lock with an owner initialized to no holder and a nesting counter, implying single holder reentrant protection for nested traps.

Update proceeds through skip decision, fresh header preparation, destination lookup, size validation, local mapping, global invalidation, cache flushing copy, restoration, unmapping and scratch release, aborting to release on any failure.

Boot parsing first handles timer, then interrupt controllers and processors, then wake mailbox; top level early setup maps, verifies, unflattens and unmaps the blob before installing this parser when appropriate.
Entry validates stack size at build time, then performs capture, task restore, entry refresh, interrupt marking, frame synthesis, delegation and terminal panic in strict order with no return path.
Reading high frames from a wider paging mode under narrow paging could alias low memory by cropping bits; the legacy path rejects such frames with a fault status.
If rebuilt headers exceed reservation or destination mapping fails, the update aborts without touching the live image; the image is cleared during copy to block concurrent use and restored after.
Misaligned or mis sized mailbox regions are ignored rather than used; when a valid mailbox is accepted, processor offlining is disabled because the two features are incompatible.
Original page table base is not preserved across task switch in this mode, so reconstructing return state would race and mishandle isolation; the handler therefore never returns.
Address wrap during firmware import stops further processing with an error to avoid corrupting the map; an empty import signals the caller to try another source.
Interrupt allocation rejects requests with too few firmware cells or with a trigger index beyond the known table, preventing out of bounds interpretation.
Wake mailbox size and alignment are each four kilobytes, namely 0x1000.
PCI memory start sentinel retains placeholder pattern 0xaeedbabe until later initialization overwrites it.
Exception stack labels map dedicated indices to short tags for double fault, nonmaskable, debug, machine check and two virtualization stacks.
Early platform matching recognizes three compatible identifiers for the CE platform plus generic bus kinds, used to probe the platform bus after tree population.
Global oops counter and saved register snapshot support repeated fatal handling and summary reporting.
Pointer sanity helper tests membership in the kernel direct map window; task state accessor reads the named field from the current processor task area.
Hotplug log prefix marks messages emitted from the crash hotplug path.
